The '''1948 FA Charity Shield''' was the 26th [[FA Community Shield|Charity Shield]], an annual English association football match played between the winners of the previous season's [[The Football League|Football League]] and [[FA Cup]]. It was the first edition held since the postponement of football during the Second World War. The match, held at [[Arsenal Stadium|Highbury]] on 6 October 1948, was contested by [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], champions of the [[1947–48 Football League]] and [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], who beat [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]] in the [[1948 FA Cup Final|final]] of the [[1947–48 FA Cup]]. This was Arsenal's eighth Charity Shield appearance to Manchester United's third.

Watched by a crowd of over 30,000, [[Reg Lewis (footballer)|Reg Lewis]], [[Bryn Jones (footballer, born 1912)|Bryn Jones]], and [[Ronnie Rooke]] each scored for the league champions inside the first 15 minutes. Manchester United responded by scoring twice before the half-time break through [[Jack Rowley]] and [[Ronnie Burke]]. [[Lionel Smith (footballer)|Lionel Smith]]'s own goal in the 53rd minute made the scoreline 4–3, and though United's attack were dominant in the second half, there were no further goals. Arsenal were awarded the Shield by [[A.V. Alexander]], the [[Secretary of State for Defence|Minister of Defence]]. Gate receipts for the match came to a total of [[Pound sterling|£]]4,300.

==Background==
The [[FA Charity Shield]] was founded in 1908 as a successor to the [[Sheriff of London Charity Shield]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Abandonment of the Sheriff Shield |page=11 |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |date=19 April 1908}}</ref> It was a contest between the respective champions of the [[The Football League|Football League]] and [[Southern Football League|Southern League]], and then by 1913 teams of amateur and professional players.<ref>{{cite news |title=The F.A. Charity Shield |page=10 |newspaper=The Times |date=7 October 1913}}</ref> In 1921, it was played by the Football League champions and [[FA Cup]] winners for the first time.<ref>{{cite news |first=Peter |last=Ferguson |title=The Shield: From the beginning |url=http://www.mcfc.co.uk/news/team-news/archive/2011/august/community-shield-2011/the-shield-from-the-beginning |work=mcfc.co.uk |publisher=Manchester City FC |date=4 August 2011 |access-date=21 April 2014 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304192421/http://www.mcfc.co.uk/news/team-news/archive/2011/august/community-shield-2011/the-shield-from-the-beginning |url-status=dead }}</ref> After a ten-year absence due to the [[Association football during World War II|suspension of football during the Second World War]], the Charity Shield made a return in 1948.<ref>{{cite web |first=James |last=Ross |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/engsupcuphist.html |title=England – List of FA Charity/Community Shield Matches |publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation (RSSSF) |date=6 August 2015 |access-date=6 March 2016}}</ref>

Arsenal qualified for the 1948 FA Charity Shield as winners of the [[1947–48 Football League]] First Division.<ref name="todayf"/> It was the club's sixth league title and striker [[Ronnie Rooke]] scored 33 goals in the campaign to become the division's top goalscorer.<ref>{{cite web |title=GGM 44 Whittaker leads Arsenal to sixth title |url=http://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/ggm-44-whittaker-leads-arsenal-to-sixth-title |publisher=Arsenal F.C |date=8 August 2007 |access-date=6 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160316025507/http://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/ggm-44-whittaker-leads-arsenal-to-sixth-title |archive-date=16 March 2016 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref> The other Charity Shield place went to [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] who beat [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]] to win the [[1948 FA Cup Final|final]] of the [[1947–48 FA Cup]].<ref name="todayf"/><ref name="hardway">{{cite news |first=Barry |last=Glendenning |title=The hardest FA Cup of all |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2003/feb/05/theknowledge.sport |website=The Guardian |date=5 February 2003 |access-date=24 March 2016}}</ref> Manchester United's progress in the competition was unique as the club was drawn against teams from the First Division in every round.<ref name="hardway"/> Their home ties were staged at three different grounds as [[Old Trafford]] was being repaired from the damage sustained in the [[Manchester Blitz]].{{sfnp|White|2010|pp=17–27}}

This was Arsenal's eighth Charity Shield appearance; prior to the game they had won five Shields ([[1930 FA Charity Shield|1930]], [[1931 FA Charity Shield|1931]], [[1933 FA Charity Shield|1933]], [[1934 FA Charity Shield|1934]], [[1938 FA Charity Shield|1938]]), and lost two ([[1935 FA Charity Shield|1935]], [[1936 FA Charity Shield|1936]]). By contrast Manchester United were undefeated in the Charity Shield; the club won their previous two appearances, in [[1908 FA Charity Shield|1908]] and [[1911 FA Charity Shield|1911]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.statto.com/football/stats/england/community-shield/honours |title=English Community Shield: Honours |publisher=Statto Organisation |access-date=21 May 2014 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140713124226/http://www.statto.com/football/stats/england/community-shield/honours |archive-date=13 July 2014 }}</ref> Manchester United had beaten Arsenal 1–0 the last time the two clubs met at Highbury, for a league fixture on 30 August 1948; [[Charlie Mitten]] scored the only goal of the match.<ref>{{cite news |title=Manchester United win at Highbury |newspaper=The Times |page=2 |date=30 August 1948}}</ref>

==Match==

===Summary===
Arsenal began the quicker of the two teams. Inside a minute, a miskick by Manchester United left back [[John Aston Sr.|John Aston]] troubled his defence, and presented [[Reg Lewis (footballer)|Reg Lewis]] and Rooke with shooting opportunities.<ref name="guardian">{{cite news|title=Exciting Charity Shield game at Highbury |newspaper=The Manchester Guardian |page=2 |date=7 October 1948}}</ref> After three minutes, Arsenal took the lead; combination play from [[Jimmy Logie]] and [[Bryn Jones (footballer, born 1912)|Bryn Jones]] forced goalkeeper [[Jack Crompton]] out of his area, and ended with Jones hitting the ball high into an empty net.<ref name="guardian"/> Lewis headed in [[Archie Macaulay]]'s cross from the right to double Arsenal's lead, and the team scored their third almost immediately, when Rooke maneuvered past the United defence to shoot past Crompton.<ref name="times">{{cite news |title=A Pleasant Revival |newspaper=The Times |page=2 |date=7 October 1948}}</ref>

United regrouped and scored immediately. Charging forward, [[John Anderson (footballer, born 1921)|John Anderson]] and [[Jack Rowley]] each shot wide, before [[Johnny Morris (footballer)|Johnny Morris]]'s effort hit the post.<ref name="guardian"/> The ball rebounded to Rowley, whose shot went in past goalkeeper [[George Swindin]].<ref name="times"/> United were in full ascendancy – "Anderson and Warner were winning the ball in mid-field, and bringing it through to their forwards [...], making the Arsenal defence feel the strain," so said ''[[The Times]]'' football correspondent.<ref name="times"/> In the 35th minute however, Lewis scored his second goal of the match, beating [[Allenby Chilton]] to the ball first and going past Crompton.<ref name="guardian"/> Five minutes before half-time, United halved Arsenal's lead – a well-worked move started by Carey in his own half was finished off by Burke.<ref name="express">{{cite news |first=John |last=MacAdam |title=Lewis snaps up two in soccer 'feast' |newspaper=Daily Express |location=London |page=4 |date=7 October 1948}}</ref>

Arsenal struggled to regain fluency in the second half, as their opponents dominated play. In the 53rd minute, United scored to make it 4–3; [[Charlie Mitten]]'s flick in the area was diverted into the Arsenal net by [[Lionel Smith (footballer)|Lionel Smith]] for an own goal.<ref name="express"/> United fashioned further chances through Burke and Rowley, but for large periods of the second half the Arsenal defence stood firm.<ref name="guardian"/> Jones' headed goal was rule out for offside, after which the match descended into a contest between United's attack and Arsenal's defence.<ref name="guardian"/> [[Jimmy Delaney]] came closest to equalising late on, when he darted forward and missed by inches.<ref name="guardian"/>

==Post-match==
[[AV Alexander, 1st Earl Alexander of Hillsborough|A.V. Alexander]], the [[Secretary of State for Defence|Minister of Defence]] presented Arsenal with the Shield.<ref name="times"/> Assessing the match the next day, ''[[Daily Express]]'' football correspondent John MacAdam wrote: "Charity begins at home, they say, and, by golly, it began at Highbury yesterday, for Arsenal were the luckiest team in the world to beat Manchester United 4–3 in the F.A. Charity Shield match between the winners of the League and the Cup."<ref name="express"/> ''The Times'' correspondent assessed, "Arsenal won because they sneaked a commanding lead of three goals, before Manchester had realised they were in London," and concluded the piece with the sentence "It had been a game worthy of the occasion and of two fine clubs."<ref name="times"/> Gate receipts for the match totalled [[Pound sterling|£]]4,300.<ref name="express"/>

Manchester United ended the season as runners-up to [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]] in the [[1948–49 Football League#First Division|Football League First Division]], and reached the semi-final stage of the FA Cup.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.stretfordend.co.uk/seasons/season1949.html |title=Manchester United Season 1948/49 |access-date=15 January 2012 |publisher=StretfordEnd.co.uk }}</ref> Arsenal progressed no further than the fourth round of the cup competition, and finished sixth in the league.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.statto.com/football/teams/arsenal/1948-1949 |title=Arsenal 1948–49 |publisher=Statto Organisation |access-date=6 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160322204801/http://www.statto.com/football/teams/arsenal/1948-1949 |archive-date=22 March 2016 |url-status=live |df=dmy-all }}</ref> The two clubs next faced each other in the Charity Shield in [[1993 FA Charity Shield|1993]], when Manchester United won the inaugural [[Premier League]] title, and Arsenal were FA Cup winners in the [[1992–93 in English football|1992–93]] season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Scots with little room for charity |first=Russell |last=Thomas |page=19 |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |date=7 August 1993}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.statto.com/football/teams/manchester-united/arsenal/head-to-head |title=Manchester United's head-to-head comparison with Arsenal |publisher=Statto Organisation |access-date=24 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160316230939/http://www.statto.com/football/teams/manchester-united/arsenal/head-to-head |archive-date=16 March 2016 |url-status=live |df=dmy-all }}</ref>
